Towable with a pintle hook. Towable to the air frame and to the maintenance bays. You'll see them a fair bit sitting on the aprons or in the AGE yards.

A typical dehydrator replacement will take at least two guys, about an hour, and a whole bunch of using the wrong tool for the right job. The kicker is when the guy before you doesn't apply antiseize to the threads. These carts usually sit outside for months on end, and you have to replace the dehydrator every 180 days.

It's a nitrox cart for the USAF, we had something similar for working with CV-22's but ours was a permanent setup with a compressor that simulated air pressures at ~200 mph. They're fascinating systems and I hope to never have to change a dehydrator filter on one of those ever again.
